claims.feature: other: flash-forward over a whole life
claims.claim: Capossere describes a quick in-and-out flash forward tied to a character the narration has just been close to, telling in one sentence what that character would remember all his life.
claims.quote: a simple, quick in and out flash forward

claims.claim: Capossere says a favourite element of Kay's writing is the refusal to denote characters as lesser or minor, viewing them instead as characters in their own story.
claims.quote: view them as characters in their own story

claims.claim: Capossere writes that Written on the Dark is not a seamless narrative but more a series of situations, pausing on a time and then jumping ahead over intervening months or years.
claims.quote: not a seamless narrative but more a series of situations

claims.claim: Capossere names as a major theme the way small decisions by people overlooked by the history books - tavern poets, bartenders, guardsmen - can have major impact.
claims.quote: the tavern poets, the bartenders, the guardsmen

claims.claim: The Fantasy Book Review reviewer Floresiensis writes that there is a precision, care and subtlety to each and every sentence of Sailing to Sarantium.
claims.source: Floresiensis, review of Sailing to Sarantium, Fantasy Book Review (undated)
claims.quote: there is a precision, care and subtlety to each and every sentence

claims.claim: The Quill to Live blogger writes that Kay's writing style is poetic but not too dense, so passages move without requiring hours of thought to decipher.
claims.source: The Quill to Live, 'The Masters Of Prose', 7 January 2016
claims.quote: incredibly poetic but also not too dense

claims.claim: The blogger lepusdomesticus reports that the first clause of Tigana is 'Both moons were high.'
claims.quote: The first clause of the entire book is

claims.claim: lepusdomesticus objects that Tigana invents species names - trialla and grele in place of nightingales and partridges - and calls them smeerps.
lepusdomesticus argues that invented names for endemic species are distracting rather than verisimilitude-increasing, because a fantasy world will not mesh with accepted reality anyway.
lepusdomesticus says the invented species names in Tigana feel completely arbitrary because they appear to have no bearing on the plot or the rest of the story.
lepusdomesticus notes that Kay begins chapter one of Tigana with unreliable narration, which she takes as a sign that he knows more than his characters intentionally.

claims.feature: other: prologue as a false beginning
claims.claim: lepusdomesticus argues that both the Prologue and Chapter One of Tigana are false beginnings that name many characters who never reappear.
claims.quote: Chapter One of the novel are false beginnings

claims.claim: The rereader keilexandra advises going back to read the first sentence of Chapter 1 of Tigana after finishing the book.
claims.source: keilexandra, 'Tigana, by Guy Gavriel Kay (reread)', LiveJournal, 2008
claims.quote: read the first sentence of Chapter 1 after you finish the book

claims.claim: keilexandra says she loves Kay's prose while calling it overwrought as it sometimes is.
keilexandra characterises Tigana as having skilfully shifting, poetic narration.
